title: Enable Rootless Docker (Linux) and Run a Container
description: Install rootless Docker, start the daemon as a normal user, and run a container.
problemStatement:
## Objective
Set up rootless Docker on a Linux machine and experience running containers without root.

### Prerequisites
- A Linux system (VM or physical) with a non‑root user account.
- Internet access to download the installer.
- Remove any existing rootful Docker installation (optional, but recommended to avoid conflicts).

### Steps
1. Install `uidmap` package:
   ```bash
   sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y uidmap
   ```
2. Run the rootless Docker installer:
   ```bash
   curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com/rootless | sh
   ```
   This will install Docker binaries and configure systemd user service.
3. Add the following to your `~/.bashrc` (if not done automatically):
   ```bash
   export PATH=/home/$USER/bin:$PATH
   export DOCKER_HOST=unix:///run/user/$(id -u)/docker.sock
   ```
   Then reload: `source ~/.bashrc`.
4. Start the Docker daemon:
   ```bash
   systemctl --user start docker
   ```
   Check status: `systemctl --user status docker`.
5. Verify the daemon is running as your user:
   ```bash
   ps aux | grep dockerd
   ```
   (it should show your username, not root).
6. Run a test container:
   ```bash
   docker run --rm hello-world
   ```
7. Run Nginx on a high port (since low ports are not allowed without configuration):
   ```bash
   docker run -d --name web-rootless -p 8080:80 nginx:alpine
   curl localhost:8080
   ```
8. Clean up:
   ```bash
   docker stop web-rootless
   docker rm web-rootless
   systemctl --user stop docker
   ```

### Deliverable
Show the output of `ps aux | grep dockerd` (non‑root user) and the successful `hello-world` output.
hints: If `systemctl --user` doesn't work, you may need to enable lingering: `sudo loginctl enable-linger $USER`.
If the installer complains about `newuidmap` or `newgidmap`, ensure the `/etc/subuid` and `/etc/subgid` files have entries for your user (the script usually handles this).
expectedOutput: `ps aux | grep dockerd` shows the daemon running under your username. `docker run hello-world` prints the hello message.
solutionCode:
sudo apt install -y uidmap
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com/rootless | sh
export PATH=/home/$USER/bin:$PATH
export DOCKER_HOST=unix:///run/user/$(id -u)/docker.sock
systemctl --user start docker
ps aux | grep dockerd
docker run --rm hello-world
docker run -d --name web-rootless -p 8080:80 nginx:alpine
curl localhost:8080
docker stop web-rootless
docker rm web-rootless
systemctl --user stop docker
